title: Edge AI and IoT-Powered System for Early Tomato Disease Detection and Smart Control
summary: MUST reports a tomato-disease detection pilot using edge AI. Avoided crop losses, higher yields, and reduced pesticide use remain unmeasured.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: MUST reports a tomato-disease detection pilot using edge AI. Avoided crop losses, higher yields, and reduced pesticide use remain unmeasured. University demonstration-farm pilot.
purpose: Detect tomato diseases early and deliver practical alerts to farmers.
system: Edge AI and IoT tomato-disease detection system
developer: Mbeya University of Science and Technology

ratings.reason: Smallholder farmers are intended to preserve crops and income.
Agricultural operators are intended to detect disease sooner; no measured field benefit is documented.
Food security and ecosystem protection are intended, without an attributable outcome.

ai_role.statement: The chapter describes this system as supporting the stated purpose. Its causal contribution to the benefit has not been separately assessed.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 5: Edge AI and IoT-Powered System for Early Tomato Disease Detection and Smart Control

produced_by: Causal conditions are not established separately in the extracted chapter.
must_hold: Farm imagery and an edge device running the disease model
Farmer-facing alerts and a mobile interface

headline: Edge AI detects tomato diseases on a demonstration farm

revisions.change: Added the sourced case with separate benefit depth, beneficiary, evidence confidence, and outcome status assessments.

claim_basis: The makers' report is on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
